Gomez - Correspondent / @carlagomezINQ Inquirer Visayas / 02:21 AM November 17, 2026 Share: BACOLOD CITY, NEGROS OCCIDENTAL, Philippines — A total of 5,236 voter applications were processed in the Negros Island Region (NIR) during the first week of voter registration from Nov. 10 to 14.
Female applicants outnumbered male applicants, with 2,800 women and 2,436 men registering, based on data from the Commission on Elections (Comelec)-NIR.
Negros Occidental recorded the highest number of applications at 3,345, comprising 1,534 males and 1,811 females.
Negros Oriental followed with 1,765 applications (829 males and 936 females), while Siquijor recorded 126 (73 males and 53 females).
READ: Comelec eyes exceeding 3-million voter registration target
Meanwhile, the poll body’s Register Anywhere Program (RAP) accommodated 40 applicants across the region, evenly split between 20 males and 20 females.
Bacolod City accounted for 35 RAP applications, including 20 males and 15 females, while Dumaguete City recorded five female applicants. No RAP applications were recorded in Siquijor during the first week.
Voter registration resumed on Nov. 10, 2026, and will continue until July 30, 2027, ahead of the 2028 National and Local Elections.
READ: Registering to vote in 2028? Here’s what you need to know
Comelec-NIR Regional Director Lionel Marco Castillano earlier said the agency is targeting a 5-percent increase in the region’s current base of more than three million registered voters, or approximately 150,000 additional registrants across the three provinces.
Eligible citizens may apply for first-time registration, transfer of voter records, reactivation, and correction of entries at their local Offices of the Election Officer, satellite and mall registration sites, or through RAP.
Comelec officials urged eligible voters to register early to avoid long queues as the deadline approaches. /cb
